name: Gas fireplace, insert or wall heater

combustion.note: Direct-vent (sealed) and B-vent units send exhaust outside (NRCan gas fireplaces). Vent-free logs and heaters, sold in the US but not approved in Canada, put it all in the room: CO alarm, open a window. Figures are gas input; millivolt units need no power, blowers and electronic ignition do.

comps.spec: Thermopile in the pilot flame: makes the millivolts that run the gas valve, wall switch, remote or thermostat with no house power (millivolt models)
comps.loc: Beside the pilot, under the logs at the burner

comps.spec: Thermocouple: holds the pilot gas valve open only while the pilot burns
comps.loc: Beside the pilot, next to the thermopile

comps.spec: Gas control valve with OFF/PILOT/ON knob and regulator (millivolt) or an electronic valve. Stays on the gas line: taking it off means breaking gas joints
comps.loc: Behind the lower grille or louvre, in the valve compartment

comps.spec: Piezo push-button igniter on millivolt models; spark electrode and ignition module on electronic models
comps.loc: Valve compartment, wired to the pilot

comps.spec: Heat-resistant glass front in a gasketed frame (ceramic on some models). Can reach 260–540 °C (500–1,000 °F) in use. Never run the fireplace without it
comps.loc: Front, held by latches or a frame

comps.spec: Convection blower on many models, runs on mains power so it doesn't run in a power cut (Travis 864 ST)
comps.loc: Under the firebox, behind the lower grille

comps.spec: Snap-disc heat switch that turns the blower on once the firebox is warm
comps.loc: On the firebox near the blower

comps.spec: Ceramic logs, cast brick panels or ceramic firebacks lining the firebox. Placed to the maker's diagram: moved logs can block the burner
comps.loc: Inside the firebox, behind the glass

comps.spec: Vent pipe to outside: direct-vent units have an exhaust pipe and a combustion-air intake (3 in each on the Regency Gi25LE); B-vent units use a single vent
comps.loc: Behind or above the firebox, through the wall or roof

comps.spec: Steel firebox, outer case and surround
Electronic ignition module and remote receiver, some with a battery backup (electronic-ignition models)
Oxygen-depletion sensor at the pilot: shuts the gas off if oxygen falls. On vent-free units, which aren't approved in Canada (Regency ventless). Not a CO alarm

buildings.loc: Living room, family room, basement rec room

notes: A standing-pilot (millivolt) gas fireplace keeps heating in a power cut: the pilot makes its own power for the valve and switch, and only the blower stops. Electronic-ignition units need mains power or a battery pack (Heatilator battery backup). Leave the gas valve and pipes connected: a removed fireplace leaves an open gas line that must be capped by someone qualified. Don't rearrange the logs or add stones or glass: material on the burner caused a delayed ignition that blew a fireplace's glass into a room in BC (TSBC fireplace incident). The glass front can burn a child badly, so keep children back or fit a barrier, and never run it with the glass cracked or removed (CPSC glass 2013; Travis 864 ST).
